perf(cluster): accelerate FULL sync and replica startup (#83)

* Reduce native follower reconnect delay to 100 ms

* perf(replication): pipeline partition handoffs

Remove per-partition stop-and-wait from native FULL synchronization. Track
NotSent/InFlight/Acked progress before sending, dispatch exact ACKs through
one reader, and require every physical partition to finish before the cut.

Run bounded independent target handoffs and join them before attempt cleanup.
Preserve same-partition dependencies and reset/cut barriers. Serialize only
complete ACK frame writes with a worker-local coroutine mutex, since short
writes can suspend; frame encoding stays outside that scope. Cancel the
whole session on reader/task failures to release cross-flow barriers.

Keep wire formats unchanged and use existing session recovery instead of
per-partition retries. Document completion, compatibility and lifetime rules.

Validate 54 focused unit tests, 52 manager integration tests, both rebuild
protocol/failure gates, and mixed old/new source-target cut/reconnect tests.
The new out-of-order regression test fails with the old serial source.
Twelve alternating cluster trials pass. Debug empty FULL median decreases
from 2.122s to 1.706s; FULL fallback from 2.066s to 1.676s. Ordinary controlled
failover uses partial continuation and shows no demonstrated speedup.

Related: #46, #70

* perf(replication): skip empty database scans during FULL

Export only DB0 in cluster mode and preserve all logical DBs for standalone
replication. Skip an empty baseline atomically on its owning worker only
when no UNSTARTED write admission remains; later writes use the publish FIFO.
Scan after pending admissions drain instead of trusting an earlier empty mask.

Replace the two per-64-partition fixed fairness sleeps with Yield. Preserve
condition polling, retry pacing and actual deadline timers.

Validate storage admission races, post-skip publication, standalone DB15 and
stale-key removal, plus cluster manager/protocol/failure gates. Three alternating
Debug trials reduce empty FULL median from 1.7305 s to 0.5250 s versus the saved
asynchronous-handoff build. Update replication architecture and public API docs.

Refs #83

* perf(cluster): overlap startup and bound Meta retry delays

Launch Meta peers and Data processes without per-process readiness waits,
then join the two replica populations behind one READY barrier. Keep replica
assignment commits ordered for topology CAS and preserve Owner-only creation.

Replace exponential Meta reconnect backoff with stateless 80-120 ms jitter
for startup and established-session loss, where lost control prevents serving.
Retain the 10-second legacy observation grace for rolling-upgrade safety.

Reuse the existing candidate-source observation wait before repeated controlled
failover: local replay may precede its next Meta heartbeat. Update the control
architecture, operations guide and retry policy test.

Validate 10 focused unit tests and seven integration scenarios, including
controlled/FULL fallback, leader replacement, automatic failover and replica
restart. Final paired Debug trials reduce empty setup median from 6.307 s to
4.135 s. Release and large-fleet retry load were not benchmarked.

Refs #83

* perf(storage): initialize only DB0 indexes in cluster mode

Prepare only enabled runtime database indexes and construct them directly
with each worker's shared arena. Worker-owned contiguous arrays outlive
partition views and avoid per-partition allocation and temporary private
arenas. Standalone retains all 16 databases.

Bound maintenance, recovery, snapshots and FULL cleanup by enabled DBs.
Preserve 16-slot durable/wire epochs and checkpoint capacities, initialize
FULL local epochs independently of index detach, and reject current records
or replay commands for disabled databases rather than hiding old data.

Add a cold/checkpoint cross-mode recovery regression and update storage and
replication architecture. Eight integration/E2E gates and 87 focused unit
tests pass. Six alternating Debug trials against 6f21997a reduce Data startup
0.808 -> 0.206 s, RSS by 58.3 MiB, and empty cluster setup 4.154 -> 3.434 s.
Release and loaded-data performance are not measured.

* fix(replication): reject full-sync counts beyond enabled databases

Validate the requested count against the runtime database count instead of
silently clamping it. Preserve smaller valid requests, including DB0-only
cluster FULL, and document the API range.

Add a regression for zero and disabled database counts. The focused unit,
standalone replication-log E2E and cluster FULL-fallback gate pass; changed
C++ lines pass clang-format and git diff --check.

* replication: restart idle history monitor after pending retirement

An idle monitor can pass its final consumer check and yield while disabling
worker logs. A concurrent native or Redis export handshake previously saw
that monitor as running before waiting for its reset. When the reset ended,
the old monitor exited and the handshake enabled history without a monitor.
Later disconnected replicas could fall behind the backlog without triggering
history retirement.

Ensure monitoring after joining a pending reset. Keep active-control/export
ownership across the wait so idle cleanup cannot retire the new consumer.
Add a deterministic fault-enabled regression for a control admitted during
idle retirement; the existing expiry/full-sync test and timeouts are intact.

* raft: fence snapshot configuration and order durable publication

RawNode restores membership when it accepts a snapshot, before older apply
jobs finish. Track that restored cut and drain covered completions without
reapplying their configuration changes. Defer local capture until snapshot
installation supplies a matching application/configuration cut, and complete
capture waiters that the incoming image has already satisfied.

Write the received image and WAL marker before raising HardState.Commit.
Anchor the snapshot commit before writing any accompanying suffix, so even a
partial suffix remains recoverable. Release WAL locks and advance GC only
after the entire transaction is durable.

Add real Runtime stale-configuration regressions and subprocess crash cuts,
including partial suffix persistence without graceful WAL close. Preserve
local snapshot commit checks and test the GC-release isolation boundary.

feat(meta): serve managed Single with committed modes and replica reads (#130)

Meta owns the immutable Single/Cluster client mode, committed in the
Topology root at creation and fixed for the deployment lifetime. Data
with Meta seeds completes a bounded bootstrap that validates mode and
serving capabilities before storage initialization (fixed 100 ms
retry); obsolete local mode/management switches return migration
guidance. No-seed standalone and Redis/Redis Cluster followers remain
supported, and managed nodes reject REPLICAOF and other external role
directives. Unauthorized bootstrap identities receive no committed
topology or service metadata.

Managed Single serves DB0 operations through the same Group authority
lifecycle as Cluster (Recovery, Prepare, Promote/Activate, Follow
Owner); one Group covers all slots. Owner reads and writes require a
live finite lease; complete replicas serve ordinary reads without
READONLY, and replica-serve-stale-data defaults to yes with CONFIG
GET/SET support. Nonzero databases and unintegrated advanced commands
stay explicitly refused rather than falling back to non-Meta paths.

Replication: contiguous completed events are acknowledged with
negotiated ACK ranges (legacy frame fallback preserved), and ready ACK
frames batch into single socket writes.

Request-path admission uses worker-local caches keyed on exact
topology/authority publication fingerprints: successful Single read
verdicts skip snapshot walks, the lease clock is sampled lazily
(replica stale reads consume population authority with no Owner lease
clock), and write rechecks compare admission fingerprints before
borrowing snapshots.

Verified against the pre-removal non-Meta native pair with controlled
interleaved benchmarks: Owner SET P1/P16/1KiB +7.4%/+16.9%/+5.3% with
p99 -20%/-29%; Owner reads at parity; managed replica reads faster
than the historical baseline. Full software suite green (CTest, large
native List/Hash/RDB, Valkey TCL) plus the dual-mode recovery/fault
matrix.

Add Lavik Admin with shared CLI management and Docker quick start (#155)

* Implemented Lavik Admin, running at localhost:4173.

  It includes:

  - Valkey-style dashboard, topology, key browser, command console, and slow logs.
  - Shared fleet database and operation tracking with lavik-ctl.
  - Cluster initialization, controlled failover, and replica expansion/shrink using already-running nodes.
  - Docker packaging and persistent storage.

  Get the login token:

  docker exec lavik-admin-dev cat /data/admin-workspace-v2/token

  Verified on this Mac with Docker: 6 browser workflows, 11 Admin tests, native regression/protocol checks, and persistence across container replacement passed.

  Limitation: resizing currently adds/removes replicas within existing primary groups. Changing primary-group count requires online data migration, which Lavik does not
  yet implement.

  Setup, compatibility requirements, and verification guide (docs/operations/lavik-admin.md)

* I added a three-node Docker quick start (admin/quickstart/README.md) and verified initialization and restart on this Mac.

  It runs one primary + two replicas, plus three Meta voters and Admin—seven containers on one machine. Docker starts the processes; you initialize the cluster through
  Admin.

  1. Prepare the new machine.

     Install Git and Docker with Compose. On Mac, use Docker Desktop.

     Copy this updated checkout, or use a branch containing the newly added admin/quickstart/ files. From the repository root:

     git submodule update --init bycorf third_party/mimalloc
     git -C bycorf submodule update --init third_party/liburing third_party/abseil

     docker build -f admin/Dockerfile.toolchain -t lavik-admin-toolchain:local .
     docker compose -f admin/quickstart/compose.yaml run --rm build

     The first build can take several minutes. No compiler or Node installation is needed on the host.

  2. Start the containers and get your login token.

     docker compose -f admin/quickstart/compose.yaml up -d
     docker compose -f admin/quickstart/compose.yaml exec admin \
       cat /data/lavik-admin/token

     Open http://localhost:4173 and enter the token.

  3. Initialize through Lavik Admin.

     Click Connect cluster and enter:

      Field                 Value
     ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━  ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
      Cluster name          demo
     ────────────────────  ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      Meta seeds            172.29.91.11:7200,172.29.91.12:7200,172.29.91.13:7200
     ────────────────────  ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      Connection profile    default

     Open Topology → Initialize cluster. Paste the contents printed by:

     cat admin/quickstart/cluster.toml

     Type demo to confirm. Wait for Healthy. Topology should show one primary and two replicas.

  4. Try a write and read.

     In Admin’s Send command view, run these separately, confirming the write:

     SET greeting "hello from Lavik"
     GET greeting

     To see the same cluster through lavik-ctl:

     docker compose -f admin/quickstart/compose.yaml exec admin \
       /build/lavik-ctl --socket /data/lavik-admin/admin.sock fleet-status demo

  5. Stop and resume without losing data.

     docker compose -f admin/quickstart/compose.yaml down
     docker compose -f admin/quickstart/compose.yaml up -d

     Volumes preserve data, cluster state, and the Admin catalog. Do not initialize again or use down -v when retaining data.

  This is a local demonstration; all three nodes share one physical machine.

perf(cluster): encode control messages once per send (#157)

The control send path encoded every message payload three times
(writer admission check, queue accounting, actual write), and
heartbeats plus frame-sized DirectiveResult/NodeControlUpdate a fourth
time for a discarded size/fit probe.

EncodeMessage now returns an EncodedMessage (type + canonical payload)
that is threaded through admission accounting, the write queue, and the
frame sink, so each message is encoded exactly once per send. Callers
that already hold canonical bytes (heartbeat fit-check, frame-or-
transfer size probes, retained canonical FullDesiredState bytes) hand
them to a new pre-encoded Write overload. Frame header assembly and
sequence assignment deliberately stay at write time. Wire format and
all admission/error semantics are unchanged.

feat(cluster): admit Single cross-slot multi-key and blocking commands (#175)

Meta-managed Single now serves DB0 cross-slot multi-key commands and the
blocking List/Sorted Set family through the sole Group's authority.
Cluster keeps CROSSSLOT; transactions, scripts/Functions, keyless global
data commands, nonzero DBs, stream blocking, and WAIT stay deferred to
their own integration work.

* Reuse the existing key extraction, worker routing, and tx fan-out;
  every mutation still passes admission, per-shard validators, and the
  storage-publication precondition.
* Unify managed reads on one contract: authority is checked once at
  admission, and only the serving-generation population fence is
  revalidated after queueing, blocking, or worker hops. Write
  re-validation is unchanged.
* Reuse the retained admission proof across blocking attempts: atomic
  fingerprint loads in steady state, fresh capture only after a real
  authority change. In-flight guards cover only the concrete storage
  attempt, so dormant waiters never hold a failover drain, and a woken
  waiter whose re-admission fails terminates honestly instead of
  consuming elements.
* Share EmitClusterDecision with the blocking path so Single maps
  unavailable authority to MASTERDOWN there too.
* gate_managed_single flips to cross-slot positives; new
  gate_managed_single_blocking covers cross-worker waits, CLIENT
  UNBLOCK/timeout, Controlled Pause, controlled cutover and uncontrolled
  crash failover with active waiters, lease-expiry dormancy, drain
  non-blocking, and the Cluster CROSSSLOT counter-example.
* Docs: unified read contract, Single admission matrix, waiter
  lifecycle, and the Serving Generation glossary entry.

feat(meta): serve authoritative Sentinel topology discovery (#177)

MASTER/MASTERS and REPLICAS/SLAVES for Meta-managed Single deployments,

shape assertions, and the unknown-service null/error replies are
recorded byte-exact from a real Redis 7.2.14 sentinel.

Close remote pin admission before testing whether a sealed staging buffer can
be released. Both flush completion paths use the same helper so the last
remote unpin either precedes the zero-count check or notifies the owner;
write buffers cannot be stranded behind release_pending with no wakeup.

Initialize GET tracing before remote admission and attach it to fast hits,
misses, and errors. Preserve the original request start across fallback while
resetting per-path stages. Trace-only I/O completion records the actual CQE
time; trace-disabled builds retain the existing awaitable layout and I/O path.

and defrag payload end-to-end tests. Live trace logs contain all 1,025 requests
in each of fast miss, durable hit, and indirect-key owner fallback workloads,
with the expected remote/hit/disk ratios.
